cycle: §6.L 68th invocation — lava-api-go new-tests stream surfaced a pre-existing failure
class: §6.J / CONST-035 — QA validator bluffs its own verdict (reports StepPassed on a crashed step) on darwin/arm64
severity: high (QA-infrastructure correctness; NOT a Lava end-user-facing feature)
surface: submodules/helixqa/pkg/detector (HelixDevelopment org submodule) consumed by lava-api-go/internal/qa/validator (Phase 4-C-4 bridge adapter)
discovered_by: lava-api-go new-tests subagent reported `internal/qa/validator` has 6 pre-existing failures, UNRELATED to its 5 new tests; main agent root-caused.
confirmed_fact: `go test ./internal/qa/validator/` fails 6 tests (TestValidateStep_Failed_DriveCrashDetection, _FailedWithAutoEmit_WritesTicket, _FailedWithoutTicketGen_NoEmission, _FailedAutoEmit_CustomTicketDir, _FailedAutoEmit_WriteErrorIsNonFatal, TestCounters_AcrossMultipleSteps). Each expects Status=StepFailed for a crashed step but gets Status="passed". The 5 NEW tests added this cycle (internal/auth, internal/gutenberg, internal/observability, internal/handlers/v1, tests/contract) all PASS and are unrelated.
root_cause: CONFIRMED via captured evidence (NOT a guess per §11.4.6): the test fixture `failingDetector` points HelixQA's desktop Detector at PID 2147483647 (guaranteed-absent) expecting alive=false -> HasCrash -> StepFailed. HelixQA's `isPIDAlive` (submodules/helixqa/pkg/detector/desktop.go) detects liveness by running `exec.Command("kill", "-0", "<pid>")` via execRunner, treating a non-nil error as dead. On this macOS host `/bin/kill -0 2147483647` returns EXIT 0 (the bash builtin `kill -0 2147483647` correctly returns exit 1 with 'No such process', but the /bin/kill BINARY that exec.Command resolves does NOT validate the out-of-range PID and exits 0). So isPIDAlive returns true for a dead PID -> ProcessAlive=true -> HasCrash=false -> HelixQA Validator sets StepPassed. The crash-detector cannot detect a dead process on macOS.

captured_evidence.bash_builtin: `kill -0 2147483647; echo $?` -> 'bash: kill: (2147483647) - No such process' / exit 1
captured_evidence.bin_kill_binary: `/bin/kill -0 2147483647; echo $?` -> exit 0 (NO error — the macOS /bin/kill binary accepts the absent out-of-range PID)
captured_evidence.test_run: `GOMAXPROCS=2 go test ./internal/qa/validator/` -> FAIL, 6 of N tests, all 'Status="passed"; want StepFailed'
captured_evidence.code_path: desktop.go isPIDAlive -> execRunner.Run("kill","-0",pid) -> exit 0 -> return true,nil

falsifiability_rehearsal.claim: The 6 failures are caused by /bin/kill returning 0 for the absent PID, not by the Lava adapter.
falsifiability_rehearsal.mutation: Probed `/bin/kill -0 2147483647` directly (the exact binary exec.Command resolves) — returned exit 0, confirming the detector receives no error and reports alive.
falsifiability_rehearsal.observed: The Lava adapter (internal/qa/validator/validator.go) is a faithful pass-through: result.Status comes verbatim from HelixQA's Validator. `go diff` on internal/ is 0 bytes — the adapter is unmodified. The defect is entirely in HelixQA's isPIDAlive liveness mechanism.
falsifiability_rehearsal.reverted: n/a — no production code was mutated; this is a read-only root-cause probe

remediation_owed.where: submodules/helixqa/pkg/detector/desktop.go isPIDAlive — fix belongs UPSTREAM in HelixQA (HelixDevelopment org), per CONST-051 (decoupling: no Lava context injected) + CONST-049 (constitution/submodule update pipeline).
remediation_owed.fix: Replace the `exec kill -0` liveness probe with a direct `syscall.Kill(pid, 0)` (returns ESRCH reliably cross-platform for absent PIDs) OR validate the PID range before shelling. The shell-out to /bin/kill is fragile across platforms (Linux /bin/kill vs macOS /bin/kill vs bash builtin all differ).
remediation_owed.process: Fix in HelixQA submodule -> falsifiability-rehearse in HelixQA -> push to HelixQA upstream -> bump submodules/helixqa pin in Lava parent (always-track-upstream per §6.AD Q9 waiver) -> re-run lava-api-go go test ./internal/qa/validator/ to confirm 6 -> 0 failures.
